fullText:
Summary: Singer (Sri Lanka) PLC (SINS.N0000) is still growing, but the boom is slowing: in the six months to September 2026 revenue rose 30% and profit 20%, and in the September quarter alone profit fell 6% as finance costs doubled. At Rs 75.00 the share trades at 3.9x its NAV of Rs 19.23 and 11.1x trailing earnings, while debt keeps rising (net debt now 3.5x equity) and the business used cash rather than producing it. I've cut my earnings estimate for this year, which lowers fair value to about Rs 42.30 (from Rs 45), so the price is about 77% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 36 and treat under Rs 31.70 as a strong buy.

What's new (six months to 30 September 2026, group, unaudited)
Revenue rose 30% to Rs 74.4bn and profit attributable rose 20% to Rs 3.50bn. EPS was Rs 3.00 against Rs 2.51.
September quarter alone: revenue rose 21% to Rs 35.7bn, but profit attributable fell 6% to Rs 1.36bn (EPS Rs 1.16 against Rs 1.23). The first fall in profit since the recovery began.
Why profit fell: net finance costs more than doubled (Rs 1.05bn against Rs 0.48bn in the quarter), bad-debt charges rose 51%, and the home appliances and consumer electronics businesses earned less than a year earlier.
Where the profit comes from: the finance business (Singer Finance and hire purchase) earned Rs 3.86bn of the half's Rs 9.0bn segment profit, up 52%; retail segments grew more slowly.
Debt: loans and overdrafts rose to Rs 94.5bn from Rs 82.3bn in March; net debt about Rs 86.5bn, 3.5x equity (3.4x in March). Singer Finance's public deposits rose another Rs 11bn.
Cash: operating cash flow was Rs 3.6bn negative (Rs 9.3bn negative a year earlier) as stock rose Rs 7.9bn and customer credit grew; capital spending tripled to Rs 1.65bn.
NAV per share Rs 19.23. Dividends of about Rs 0.84 a share were declared in the half (28% of profit).
A tax dispute over deemed VAT (Rs 1.19bn, 2014–2015) is still before the Court of Appeal; no provision has been made.

Price
Price: Rs 75.00 (CSE closing price, 2026-11-09). Please check it live. In April–September 2026 it traded between Rs 66.00 and Rs 92.50 (Rs 71.50–84.90 in July–September) and closed September at Rs 78.90.

Methods
NAV (Rs 19.23): 3.9x.
Return on equity: about 40% over the last 12 months, but the September quarter annualises to about 25%.
P/E: 11.1x trailing EPS of Rs 6.78.
Dividends: Rs 1.84 for 2025/26, a 2.5% yield; about Rs 0.84 declared so far this year.
Debt: net debt 3.5x equity.
Justified price to book: Rs 15.6 / 26.6 / 42.1 across the cases, weighted Rs 26.4.
P/E method: Rs 38.5 / 59.4 / 80.3, weighted Rs 57.3.
Residual income: Rs 20.1 / 39.6 / 87.0, weighted Rs 43.2.
Dividend model: Rs 10.6 / 15.5 / 22.9 (not used in the fair value).

Singer pays out under a third of its profit, so a dividend model understates it, and its cash flow is swamped by customer-credit growth, so a cash-flow DCF isn't reliable. The P/E method is the most generous; price to book is the strictest.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 21% / 19% / 17.5% (unchanged).
Long-run ROE (price to book): 18% / 24% / 30% (unchanged).
ROE path (residual income): 28% falling to 18% / 34% falling to 22% / 40% falling to 28% (starting points lowered from 30% / 38% / 42% after the weaker September quarter).
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7% (unchanged).
EPS for the year to March 2027 × P/E: 5.5 × 7 / 6.6 × 9 / 7.3 × 11 (base and bull lowered from 7.6 and 8.5). The base case assumes the second half earns about Rs 3.60, a little below last year's Rs 3.78, because profit has started to fall.
Average of the three methods: Rs 24.7 / Rs 41.9 / Rs 69.8.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 42.30 (was Rs 45), so Rs 75.00 is about 77% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 36.00 (was Rs 38.30), and 25% gives Rs 31.70 (was Rs 33.80).
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 42.30, 150 at up to Rs 36.00 and 150 at up to Rs 31.70. That averages about Rs 37.23, about Rs 18,615, against Rs 37,500 at Rs 75.00.
Realism: Rs 42.30 needs about a 44% fall. The share was Rs 29.50 as recently as April–June 2025, so cyclical falls of that size happen, but it hasn't been below Rs 66 this year.

Sensitivity (residual income base case, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 17.5%: 35.4 / 47.6 / 70.6 for long-run ROE of 18% / 22% / 28%.
Cost of equity 19%: 29.9 / 39.6 / 57.8.
Cost of equity 21%: 24.4 / 31.8 / 45.5.

Business tests: 1 of 4 passed (category 3, avoid for now, unchanged)
Return on equity: passed (about 40% over 12 months). Debt: failed (3.5x equity and rising). Steady profit: failed (loss in 2023/24; profit now falling again). Cash: failed (operating cash flow negative).

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: profit growth recovering in the December quarter (the festive season); finance costs stabilising; debt falling relative to equity; bad debts staying low; a higher payout.
Supports a lower value: another quarter of falling profit; interest rates rising; bad debts climbing after rapid credit growth; net debt above 4x equity; an adverse court ruling on the deemed-VAT case.

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2025 and March 2026 and the interim reports to September 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
